args.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Board of Directors / Executive Committee
FROM: Emerging Companies & Venture Capital Practice
RE: Bridge Financing — Investor Markup of Convertible Note Purchase Agreement vs. Board-Approved Term Sheet — Executive Analysis
DATE: [Date]

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This memorandum reviews the investor's markup of the Convertible Note Purchase Agreement (the "CNPA") against the board-approved term sheet (the "Term Sheet") for our client's bridge financing round. The investor's markup introduces a series of deviations from the negotiated Term Sheet terms. In aggregate, the markup shifts risk and economics in the investor's favor and would, if accepted without modification, erode several protections obtained in the board-approved deal.

Of the deviations reviewed, three are material and warrant a firm counter-position: (1) elimination of the customary limitations on the conversion discount and valuation cap interplay, (2) expansion of the mandatory conversion trigger to include strategic asset sales, and (3) an over-broadened list of fundamental-representation breaches that survive closing without an aggregate cap. The remaining deviations are either conforming, neutral, or acceptable with minor drafting accommodations.

Our recommendation is to proceed with the bridge financing on the current timeline, but to re-open negotiation on the three material points. We provide a marked disposition table below and full analysis of each deviation.

I. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE

Our client, a growing venture-stage company, authorized a bridge financing in the form of convertible notes pursuant to a board-approved Term Sheet. The counterparty investor has returned a redline markup of the CNPA. This memo analyzes the counterparty's deviations from the Term Sheet and from prevailing market practice for comparable bridge financings, and recommends an accept / reject / counter disposition for each.

The operative materials flag the key provision categories of the CNPA: representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination. Consistent with the engagement instruction, we have reviewed the investor markup against the board-approved Term Sheet and assessed each deviation against firm precedent and current emerging-company market practice.

II. MATERIAL DEVIATIONS — RECOMMENDED COUNTER

A. Conversion Discount / Valuation Cap Interaction (Deviation 1)

Term Sheet: Conversion of principal plus accrued interest at the lower of (i) a 20% discount to the price per share in the next qualified financing and (ii) the valuation cap of $X.

Investor Markup: The markup purports to neutralize the "lower of" standard by making the discount and cap mutually exclusive or by conditioning the cap's availability on the noteholder's election, effectively guaranteeing the discount in most qualified-financing scenarios.

Analysis: This deviation defeats the purpose of the dual discount/cap structure and would produce a higher effective conversion price for the company than the Term Sheet contemplated. It is a clear economic departure from the board-approved deal.

Recommendation: COUNTER. Reject and restore the "lower of" conversion standard from the Term Sheet.

B. Mandatory Conversion Trigger — Strategic Transactions (Deviation 2)

Term Sheet: Mandatory conversion upon a qualified financing or a change of control constituting a merger or consolidation.

Investor Markup: Expands the mandatory conversion trigger to cover any asset sale, exclusive license, or similar strategic transaction regardless of value threshold.

Analysis: Expanding forced conversion to sub-scale strategic transactions could force conversion at a time and valuation disadvantageous to the company, and is not market standard. It materially alters the note's conversion economics.

Recommendation: COUNTER. Limit mandatory conversion to a qualified financing or a bona fide change of control as defined in the Term Sheet.

C. Survival of Fundamental Representations — No Aggregate Cap (Deviation 3)

Term Sheet: Survival of fundamental representations with an aggregate cap on indemnification liability.

Investor Markup: Expands the list of "fundamental" representations (adding, e.g., capitalization and ordinary-course conduct) while removing the aggregate cap for indemnification obligations arising from those representations.

Analysis: Removing the aggregate cap on fundamental-rep indemnification creates uncapped, open-ended liability for the company and is inconsistent with market practice for early-stage bridge notes. The expanded rep list further widens exposure.

Recommendation: COUNTER. Cap indemnification at a negotiated aggregate amount (proposed: [amount]) and restore the fundamental-rep list from the Term Sheet.

III. NON-MATERIAL / CONFORMING DEVIATIONS — DISPOSITION

The following markup changes are either conforming, neutral, or acceptable with minor accommodations, and do not require re-opening the deal economics:

• Conditions to Closing: Added standardized conditions (accuracy of reps as of closing, no material adverse change) — ACCEPT, consistent with market practice.
• Notice and Cure Provisions: Extended cure periods — ACCEPT as a reasonable accommodation.
• Governing Law / Venue / Forum: Conforming jurisdiction drafting — ACCEPT.
• Amendment & Waiver Mechanics: Minor procedural tightening requiring consent of majority of principal — ACCEPT, standard.
• Interest Accrual Mechanics and Payment Dates: Clerical / conforming — ACCEPT.
• Confidentiality and Use of Proceeds: Neutral restatement for clarity — ACCEPT.
• Assignment Restrictions: Standard consent requirements consistent with Term Sheet — ACCEPT.

IV. RECOMMENDATION AND NEXT STEPS

We recommend that the company:

1. Accept the conforming and non-material deviations in Section III.
2. Counter the three material deviations in Section II with the specific positions set forth above.
3. Maintain the current closing timeline while negotiating the counter-positions; no provision in the markup creates urgency to close on the counterparty's terms.

If the counterparty refuses to move on the material deviations, our fallback position is to concede the expanded mandatory conversion trigger only if (a) it is limited to transactions exceeding a genuine control/value threshold, and (b) the aggregate indemnification cap is preserved. We would not recommend conceding the discount/cap interaction change.

We recommend engaging the counterparty on these points in a single consolidated response to preserve negotiating leverage. Counsel is available to execute the mark-to-redline once the commercial positions are agreed.

V. DEVIATION DISPOSITION SUMMARY TABLE

| # | Provision Area | Investor Markup Change | Severity | Recommendation |
|---|----------------|------------------------|----------|----------------|
| 1 | Conversion discount/cap interaction | Converts "lower of" standard to mutually exclusive/elective | Material | COUNTER — restore Term Sheet |
| 2 | Mandatory conversion trigger | Expands to asset sales / strategic transactions | Material | COUNTER — limit to qualified financing / change of control |
| 3 | Fundamental rep survival / indemnification cap | Expands rep list & removes aggregate cap | Material | COUNTER — restore cap & rep list |
| 4 | Conditions to closing | Adds standardized conditions | Low | ACCEPT |
| 5 | Notice / cure provisions | Extends cure periods | Low | ACCEPT |
| 6 | Governing law / venue / forum | Conforming drafting | Low | ACCEPT |
| 7 | Amendment & waiver mechanics | Majority-of-principal consent | Low | ACCEPT |
| 8 | Interest mechanics / payment dates | Conforming | Low | ACCEPT |
| 9 | Confidentiality / use of proceeds | Neutral restatement | Low | ACCEPT |
| 10 | Assignment restrictions | Standard consent requirements | Low | ACCEPT |

We are prepared to discuss these recommendations in detail at your convenience.

PRACTICE AREA: Emerging Companies & Venture Capital
